subject: Mismatching row sizes when creating estimation/prediction stacks

messages.author: 81d9f5c9c5092a6e
messages.subject: Mismatching row sizes when creating estimation/prediction stacks
parts:
Dear INLA Developers,

I am adapting code from the spatio-temporal analysis conducted by Paula Moraga in Ch. 10 of her Geospatial Health Data textbook. My goal is to predict seroprevalence in Haiti to malaria based on time (survey year), spatial effects, and a set of covariates using georeferenced point data; as a reminder, in her analysis, she predicted levels of air pollution in Spain, also using point data.

I was able to use Dr. Moraga's code for my own data, up until the time came to create the prediction and estimation stacks. 

For reference, my prediction dataset looks like this, with 130,940 rows corresponding to 32,735 georeferenced points per year:

 

Any covariate values with a temporal component (e.g., rain) correspond to the average for that set of coordinates in the year indicated, while static covariate values (e.g., elevation) unique to each location are simply repeated across each year for that location. It is unlikely that different coordinates were included in each year based on the method I used to obtain these covariate values (using sample raster values in QGIS). 

My observation dataset has the same structure, with 1,120 rows corresponding to 1,120 locations, which were surveyed once in a given year (2014, 2015, 2016, or 2017).

However, when I attempt to create estimation and prediction stacks, I get the following error code for both:


Can you please let me know how I might be able to resolve this error? 

This is the code I used for the stacks, if it helps:

  

I truly appreciate any help or guidance.

Thank you,

Alicia

messages.author: 81d9f5c9c5092a6e
messages.subject: Re: Mismatching row sizes when creating estimation/prediction stacks
parts: Follow-up: I was able to surmise that the projection matrices A and Ap are what have the mismatching number of rows compared to index set s. I see that both matrices are classed as a Large dgCMatrix, whereas the ones in Dr. Moraga's output were formal class dgCMatrix. However, I followed the matrix and index set construction exactly according to her code, so I am wondering what went wrong here. Again, thanks for any help!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mismatching row sizes when creating estimation/prediction stacks
parts:
Hi,

The error message indicates that there is a size mismatch between your covariate effects and the number of rows in the A-matrix.
You didn’t say which of the two stacks gives the error, but I suggest checking the inputs to both stack calls. For the first call, the data.frame for the covariates newest to have the same number of rows as the A matrix. For the second call the data.frame needs to match the number of rows in Ap.

Finn
